newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Rebels blast Colombia's main oil pipeline again.
newsitem.headline: Rebels blast Colombia's main oil pipeline again.

text.p: Leftist rebels dynamited two sections of Colombia's main oil pipeline and brought pumping operations to a standstill, the state oil company Ecopetrol said on Tuesday.
More than 2,000 barrels were spilled in the twin attack on the pipeline, which runs from the northeastern Cano Limon field to the Caribbean coast oil terminal of Covenas.
Repair work had still not begun Tuesday afternoon because of the heavy presence of National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels in the area, an Ecopetrol spokesman said.
The first attack took place Sunday and was followed by a second Monday, both in northeastern Arauca province.

The pipeline, which pumps about 200,000 barrels a day, has been dynamited more than 40 times this year alone. The bill for 80,000 barrels of spilled crude, 1.1 million barrels in lost production and the cost of damage was estimated at more than $38 million between January and September, according to a recent Ecopetrol report.
The ELN, founded by radical Roman Catholic priests in the 1960s, is Colombia's second largest guerrilla force and specialises in attacks on multinational companies and oil infrastructure.
